title: Derivative of the Mills function
statement: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ and define $F(x)=\varphi(x)(x^{-3}-x^{-1})$ for $x\ne0$. For every nonzero real $x$, $F$ is differentiable at $x$ and $F'(x)=\varphi(x)(1-3x^{-4})$.
replaced: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, let $F(0)=0$ and $F(x)=\varphi(x)(x^{-3}-x^{-1})$ for $x\ne0$, and let $H(0)=\varphi(0)$ and $H(x)=\varphi(x)(1-3x^{-4})$ for $x\ne0$. For every nonzero real $x$, the function $F$ is differentiable at $x$ with derivative $F'(x)=H(x)$.
